claims.statement: X states an OAuth 2.0 refresh token is issued only when the offline.access scope is applied, and is used to obtain a new access token without prompting the user.

sources.supports: If the scope `offline.access` is applied an OAuth 2.0 refresh token will be issued.
Refresh tokens allow an application to obtain a new access token without prompting the user via the refresh token flow.

claims.statement: X states the refresh token returned by the OAuth 1.0a token exchange is valid for about 6 months and single-use, and that each refresh returns a new one.

sources.supports: valid for about 6 months and single-use; each refresh returns a new one

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Format of the OAuth 2.0 refresh token is not stated on the pages read.
The lifetime is stated on the token-exchange page for tokens returned by that exchange; whether it holds for refresh tokens from the authorization code flow is not stated.
The candidate is established to exist from the pages read; its format (prefix, alphabet, length) is not researched.
